description: The Goat in the Chinese zodiac: gentleness, creativity and empathy, its Earth element, years from 1967 to 2027, and its San He, Liu He and Liu Chong matches.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Goat is the eighth animal of the twelve-year cycle, with Earth as its fixed element and Yin polarity. It is traditionally associated with gentleness, creativity and empathy. Your animal follows the Lunar New Year of your birth, so early-year birthdays can belong to the previous animal.

sections.heading: The Goat in Chinese astrology
paragraphs: The Goat is the eighth animal of the cycle, and the same character is also translated as Sheep or Ram. It is usually described as gentle, creative and compassionate. Its branch, Wei, is linked with late summer, and its fixed element is Earth. People born in Goat years are often portrayed as artistic, kind and sensitive, with a rich inner life and a love of beauty and comfort. The Goat is associated with harmony and with a preference for cooperation over competition. Descriptions also mention worry, indecision and a need for reassurance. Many readings present the Goat as someone who flourishes in a supportive environment and who brings warmth and imagination to the people and places around it.

Many readers recognise the Goat in a gift for creating atmosphere, whether through decorating a room, cooking a meal or simply listening well. As a Yin animal, its strength is receptive and nurturing, and it often senses how others are feeling before they say so.

sections.heading: The Goat at work
paragraphs: At work, the Goat is often described as creative, considerate and good at collaborative work. The arts, design, music, writing, care professions, gardening and hospitality are commonly mentioned, along with roles that value imagination and empathy. A Goat tends to work best when it feels supported and appreciated. The traditional caution is vulnerability to pressure: a Goat may struggle in harsh, competitive environments or find it hard to make decisions without encouragement. Readings often suggest that people born in Goat years seek out teams with a kind culture and clear structure, and that they build confidence by finishing creative work regularly and letting it be seen rather than holding it back until it feels perfect.

A Goat also tends to do well with a mentor or manager who offers encouragement and clear direction. Recognition matters to it, not for status but as reassurance that its contribution is valued, and that reassurance often unlocks its most original work.

sections.heading: The Goat in relationships
paragraphs: In relationships, the Goat is usually described as affectionate, devoted and romantic, with a deep need for emotional security. A Goat often expresses love through care, creativity and attention to a partner's comfort. Its classical allies are its San He partners, the Rabbit and the Pig, and its Liu He secret friend, the Horse, while the Ox sits opposite it in the six clashes. The common relationship friction is dependence or moodiness: a Goat may rely heavily on a partner for reassurance or withdraw when it feels criticised. Partners who are steady, gentle and encouraging tend to help a Goat feel secure, which allows its warmth and imagination to come forward.

Friendships with a Goat are often tender and loyal. It tends to be thoughtful with gifts and generous with time, and it values friends who are kind and patient in return. A Goat often keeps friendships for many years and may be the one who remembers shared history most vividly.

sections.heading: Years of the Goat and their elements
paragraphs: Recent and upcoming years of the Goat are 1967 (Fire), 1979 (Earth), 1991 (Metal), 2003 (Water), 2015 (Wood) and 2027 (Fire). Each begins at Lunar New Year rather than on January 1, so people born in January or early February need to check the date: in 1967, for example, the Goat year began on February 9, and anyone born before that is a Fire Horse. The element attached to each year comes from the ten-year cycle of heavenly stems, so a Fire Goat and a Earth Goat share the animal's core character but differ in flavour. Separately, the Goat always carries Earth as its fixed element and a Yin polarity, which describe the animal itself. Because the five stem elements and twelve animals line up again only every sixty years, the Metal Goat of 1991 returns in 2051. The Chinese zodiac calculator on this site applies the Lunar New Year table from 1924 to 2044 automatically.

sections.heading: Growth edges for the Goat
paragraphs: The growth edge for the Goat usually involves confidence and self-reliance. Traditional descriptions mention worry, indecision, sensitivity to criticism and a tendency to avoid conflict. A Goat may also wait for others to take the lead rather than trusting its own judgment. Practices that tend to help include making small decisions independently, sharing creative work before it feels finished, and developing routines that provide security from within. The Goat's gift is gentleness and imagination, the ability to create beauty and comfort for others. It tends to grow when that gentleness is joined by a stronger sense of its own voice, so that kindness becomes a strength rather than a reason to stay quiet.

In a Unified Reading, the Goat often adds a note of gentleness and imagination to the wider profile, softening a driven Life Path or Sun sign, or deepening the creativity of an expressive one. For anyone born in a Goat year, these growth notes are prompts for reflection rather than fixed traits.

faq.question: Is it the Year of the Goat or the Sheep?
faq.answer: Both. The Chinese character yang covers goats and sheep, so English sources use Goat, Sheep or Ram. They all refer to the same eighth animal of the cycle.

faq.question: What is the Goat's personality in Chinese astrology?
faq.answer: Gentle, creative, compassionate and sensitive. The Goat is often described as artistic and kind, with a love of harmony and a need for emotional security.

faq.question: What years are the Year of the Goat?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044 the Goat years are 1931, 1943, 1955, 1967, 1979, 1991, 2003, 2015, 2027 and 2039. Each starts at Lunar New Year, which falls between January 21 and February 20.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Goat?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Rabbit and Pig share the Goat's San He trine and the Horse is its Liu He secret friend. The Ox (Liu Chong) and the Rat (Liu Hai) are the pairings readings treat as needing more care.
